name: Efai
title: Merarite Levite in David's time
summary: Efai (also spelled Ephai or Ofi) is a biblical figure mentioned to a limited extent in Scripture. In 1 Chronicles, Efai is listed as one of the descendants associated with the tribe of Judah and Caleb. The name also appears in Jeremiah 40, where 'the sons of Efai from Netophah' are noted among the military leaders who came to Gedaliah after the fall of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The sons of Efai come to Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: After Babylon's destruction of Jerusalem, the sons of Efai from Netophah joined other military leaders in coming to Gedaliah, who had been appointed governor over those remaining in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Gedaliah promises safety
keyEvents.description: Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, swore to the sons of Efai and the other commanders that they could safely serve the Chaldeans and live in the land.

keyEvents.title: Warning about Ishmael's conspiracy
keyEvents.description: Johanan and other military leaders, including the sons of Efai, warned Gedaliah that Baalis, king of Ammon, had sent Ishmael to kill him, but Gedaliah did not believe them.

keyEvents.title: The Murder of Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed Gedaliah and those who were with him in Mizpah, which affected the group to which the sons of Ephai belonged.

keyEvents.title: Flight to Egypt
keyEvents.description: After Gedaliah's death, the survivors, including the sons of Ephai, feared Babylonian revenge and went down to Egypt against the prophet Jeremiah's advice.
